commits.edited_message:
pcre2posix: do not truncate the subject length to int in regexec (#1022)

Co-authored-by: Manohar Paturi <manoharpaturi@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

posix: validate REG_STARTEND offsets and NULL pointer arguments (#1009)

With the offsets now known to be ordered, pass the start offset to
pcre2_match() directly instead of adjusting the subject pointer by
hand; the reported pmatch offsets are then the ovector values as
returned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect is a heap over-read in pcre2_match() reached through regexec() with REG_STARTEND, and it exists only in the composition of the two edited commits. regexec() passes pcre2_match() a (subject pointer, length, start offset) triple that is self-consistent only if exactly one adjustment is applied to the subject: either the pointer is bumped by rm_so and the length is (eo - so), or the pointer is left alone and rm_so is passed as PCRE2's native start offset with eo as the total length. Commit abbf6915 (while widening so/eo to PCRE2_SIZE) hoists the pointer bump into the REG_STARTEND branch (`string += so;`) and simplifies the call to (string, eo - so, 0) — correct for the call it leaves behind. Commit 2d3a98a9 (while adding the offset validation) switches the call to the native start-offset convention (string, eo, so) and drops the now-redundant `+ so` re-adjustment in the pmatch write-back — correct only because, in the tree it was written against, `string` is still the original, un-bumped pointer. In the combined tree the pointer is advanced by rm_so (first commit) AND eo is passed as the subject length with rm_so again as the start offset (second commit), so pcre2_match() scans up to string + rm_so + rm_eo — i.e. rm_so code units past the caller-declared end string + rm_eo. With in-contract input (0 < rm_so < rm_eo = exact malloc'd buffer size, non-NUL-terminated subject, which is precisely what REG_STARTEND exists for) this reads past the heap allocation and ASan reports heap-buffer-overflow in pcre2_match(). Neither single edit is reachable as a bug on its own: with only the first commit the call keeps the (bumped pointer, eo - so) pairing, and with only the second the call keeps the (un-bumped pointer, eo, so) pairing; both pairings are memory-safe (verified by building both single-edit variants: the PoC exits cleanly on each). A correct fix is non-local because neither diff is wrong in isolation: the first commit's hunk shows a self-consistent hoist, and the second commit's call-site hunk (whose context shows only the non-STARTEND branch, not the bump several lines above) shows a self-consistent switch to the start-offset convention, with a matching write-back change. Restoring safety requires reconciling the branch-local pointer adjustment introduced by one commit with the call-site length convention introduced by the other — e.g. passing (eo - so) alongside the bumped pointer — a change that can only be derived by reasoning across both commits' diffs; no correction confined to a single diff's own hunks suggests itself, because each hunk is internally correct. (Note on the recorded patches: each patch is the diff of the edited commit's tree against its real counterpart, so the patch for 2d3a98a9 necessarily also shows the `string += so;` line — that hunk is the first commit's own edit, replayed on top.)

pocs.entry_point: regexec (POSIX API: regcomp/regexec with REG_STARTEND), libpcre2-posix
